items.followUp: Explain the role of photosystems I and II in non-cyclic electron transport.

rubric.why: Identifies the two photosystems involved in the Z-scheme.
rubric.description: Names Photosystem II and Photosystem I.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both photosystems.

rubric.why: Shows the direction of electron flow in the Z-scheme.
rubric.description: States that electrons flow from water through the photosystems to NADP⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct electron-flow path.

modelAnswer: The Z-scheme is the pathway of electron flow in non-cyclic photophosphorylation, involving Photosystem II and Photosystem I.
Electrons move from water through both photosystems to NADP⁺; their energy level changes give the pathway a Z-shaped appearance.

items.followUp: What is the main respiratory substrate used by cells to release energy?

rubric.why: Identifies glucose or carbohydrates as the main respiratory fuel.
rubric.description: Names glucose as the main fuel used in respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for glucose or carbohydrates.

rubric.why: Recognizes that respiratory fuels come from food molecules.
rubric.description: States that food molecules provide fuel for respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying food or organic compounds as the source.

modelAnswer: The main fuel used in respiration is glucose, obtained from food.
Other food molecules, such as fats and proteins, may also be used as respiratory fuels.

items.followUp: How do enzymes speed up chemical reactions?

rubric.why: Identifies the energy barrier enzymes affect.
rubric.description: States that enzymes lower the activation energy of a reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that activation energy is lowered.

rubric.why: Explains how the enzyme makes the reaction easier to occur.
rubric.description: Explains that an enzyme provides an alternative pathway, often by forming an enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an appropriate explanation of the mechanism.

modelAnswer: Enzymes bind with their substrates to form an enzyme-substrate complex.
This provides an alternative reaction pathway with lower activation energy, so the reaction occurs faster.

items.followUp: What is meant by an anabolic metabolic pathway?

rubric.why: Recognizes that a pathway consists of linked reactions.
rubric.description: Defines a metabolic pathway as a series or sequence of reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a series of reactions.

rubric.why: Includes the role of enzymes in metabolic pathways.
rubric.description: States that the reactions are controlled or catalysed by enzymes, with the product of one reaction becoming the next substrate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the enzyme role or linked-product description.

modelAnswer: A metabolic pathway is a series of linked chemical reactions in a cell.
Each reaction is catalysed by an enzyme, and the product of one reaction may become the substrate for the next.

items.followUp: Define an enzyme activator and give one example.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a cofactor as an inorganic helper component.
rubric.description: Defines a cofactor as a non-protein component, commonly an inorganic ion, required for enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a cofactor as an inorganic/non-protein helper.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a coenzyme as an organic helper component.
rubric.description: Defines a coenzyme as an organic non-protein molecule that helps an enzyme function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a coenzyme as an organic helper.

modelAnswer: A cofactor is a non-protein component, usually an inorganic ion, required for an enzyme to function.
A coenzyme is an organic non-protein molecule that assists an enzyme.

items.followUp: Give one example each of a major mineral and a trace mineral.

rubric.why: Gives the defining daily-amount distinction for major minerals.
rubric.description: States that major minerals are required in relatively large amounts, commonly more than 100 mg per day.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct amount distinction.

rubric.why: Gives the defining daily-amount distinction for trace minerals.
rubric.description: States that trace minerals are required in small amounts, commonly less than 100 mg per day.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct amount distinction.

modelAnswer: Major minerals are required by the body in relatively large amounts, generally more than 100 mg per day; examples include calcium and phosphorus.
Trace minerals are required in small amounts, generally less than 100 mg per day; examples include iron and zinc.

items.followUp: What causes atherosclerosis, and how can it affect blood flow?

rubric.why: Describes the general change to arteries in arteriosclerosis.
rubric.description: Defines arteriosclerosis as hardening or thickening of artery walls and loss of their elasticity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the general hardening or loss-of-elasticity description.

rubric.why: Identifies the plaque build-up specific to atherosclerosis.
rubric.description: Defines atherosclerosis as the build-up of fatty or cholesterol-rich plaques in artery walls.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the plaque build-up distinction.

modelAnswer: Arteriosclerosis is the general hardening and thickening of artery walls, which causes them to lose elasticity.
Atherosclerosis is a type of arteriosclerosis in which fatty or cholesterol-rich plaques build up in the inner walls of arteries.

items.followUp: Describe how cells are organized into tissues and organs in a multicellular organism.

rubric.why: Describes the cellular organization of unicellular organisms.
rubric.description: States that a unicellular organism consists of one cell that carries out life processes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the one-cell description.

rubric.why: Describes the cellular organization of multicellular organisms.
rubric.description: States that a multicellular organism consists of many cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the many-cells description.

rubric.why: Explains how cells are organized functionally in multicellular organisms.
rubric.description: States that cells in multicellular organisms may become specialized for particular functions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specialization or division of labour.

rubric.why: Gives the higher levels of organization formed by cells.
rubric.description: Describes the organization of specialized cells into tissues, organs, and organ systems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct sequence of organizational levels.

modelAnswer: Organisms are cellularly organized as unicellular or multicellular.
A unicellular organism consists of one cell, which performs all the life processes.
A multicellular organism consists of many cells, often specialized for different functions.
Specialized cells are organized into tissues, tissues into organs, and organs into organ systems.
